 Hindustan Aeronautics Set to Deliver 180 Tejas Jets as IAF Targets Full Squadron
 Hindustan Aeronautics Limited faces a critical execution milestone as the Indian Air Force targets full squadron induction of LCA Mk1A fighters by the end of FY27. Backed by 180 ordered Tejas jets and ongoing Su-30 MKI upgrades, execution on deliveries remains key to revenue conversion.
 Sahi Markets Published: 16 Nov 2026, 10:36 AM IST (2 days ago) Last Updated: 16 Nov 2026, 10:36 AM IST (2 days ago) 2 min read Reviewed by Arpit Seth Share Market snapshot: The Indian Air Force confirmed that procurement of 180 LCA Tejas fighters is underway alongside ongoing Su-30 MKI upgrades. Induction of the LCA Mk1A variant is set to begin shortly, aiming to operationalize a full squadron by the end of the current financial year.
 Data Snapshot
 Order pipeline includes 180 LCA Tejas aircraft contractually committed for Indian Air Force induction.
 Full-year FY26 revenue reached ₹32,250 crore compared to ₹30,981 crore in the previous fiscal year.
 Total order book stood at ₹2.54 lakh crore at the end of FY26, representing 7.5 times trailing twelve-month revenue.
 What's Changed
 LCA Mk1A transition moves from assembly testing to active squadron induction within FY27.
 FY26 standalone revenue expanded to ₹32,250 crore from ₹30,981 crore YoY.
 Key Takeaways
 The IAF has reaffirmed orders for 180 Tejas fighter aircraft alongside Prachand helicopter programs.
 LCA Mk1A induction will begin imminently, targeting a complete squadron operationalized by the end of the financial year.
 Su-30 MKI fleet upgrades continue in parallel, bolstering HAL's long-term maintenance and overhaul revenue stream.
 SAHI Perspective
 The Indian Air Force's operational timeline places execution back at the center of valuation dynamics for HAL. With order visibility secured across 180 Tejas jets and an order book worth 7.5 times revenue, revenue recognition depends entirely on timely serial delivery without supply chain bottlenecks.
 Market Implications
 Demonstrated progress on LCA Mk1A deliveries can provide a valuation re-rating catalyst for HAL. Higher execution speed reduces working capital drag and accelerates revenue recognition from defence manufacturing.
 Trading Signals
 Market Bias: Bullish
 Strong order book visibility backed by 180 Tejas fighter orders and ₹2.54 lakh crore backlog supports long-term revenue trajectory, contingent on delivery ramp-up.
 Overweight: Defence Equipment, Aerospace Manufacturing
 Trigger Factors: 
 First batch delivery confirmation of LCA Mk1A to IAF
 Operationalization of Nashik third production line output
 Quarterly execution commentary on GE engine supply timelines
 Time Horizon: Medium-term (3-12 months)
 Industry Context
 India's defense manufacturing strategy emphasizes indigenization, with domestic production scaling toward full equipment self-reliance. Public sector aerospace platforms are leaning on private vendors for structural sub-assemblies to expand annual assembly capacity.
 Key Risks to Watch
 Supply chain delays in key imported components such as jet engines
 Integration friction or extended flight test certification schedules
 Recent Developments
 In October 2025, the Ministry of Defence inaugurated HAL's third production line for LCA Mk1A at Nashik. Private sub-assembly supply chains were established with Larsen & Toubro delivering wing sets and VEM Technologies delivering centre fuselage units.
 Closing Insight
 Execution consistency on serial aircraft production will determine whether HAL can fully capitalize on its record order book during FY27.
